BURHAN:v4p406/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p406/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p406/r1.claim: The listed ما clauses include relative ما: what is harvested and stored, what was prepared for the seven years, what fathers married, and what people worship besides God.

BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r1.claim: Abraham’s people argued about his faith and threatened that their idols would harm him if he abandoned them.
BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r1.anchor: {وحآجه قومه} أي : جادلوه في دينه وهددوه بالأصنام أن تصيبه بسوء

BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r2.claim: The emphatic form is an assimilation of two nūns in the original أتحاجونني, meaning “are you disputing with me?”
BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r2.anchor: أتحاجوانى} بنون ثقيلة أصله أتحاجونني بنونين أولاهما نون الرفع والثانية نون الوقاية

BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r3.claim: Abraham’s argument concerns God’s oneness, and he says God has guided him to truth.
BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r3.anchor: {فى الله} أي في شأنه تعالى ووحدانيته {وقد هداان} أي : والحال إن الله تعالى هداني إلى الحق.

BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r4.claim: He does not fear the idols because they have no power to cause harm.
BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r4.anchor: {ولا أخاف ما تشركون به} أي : ما تشركون به تعالى من الأصنام أن يصيبني بسوء لعدم قدرتها على شيء.

BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r5.claim: The exception is connected, with an omitted time: he fears no idol at any time unless God wills an injury through them; the idols themselves have no causal power.
BURSEVI:v3p45#2/r5.anchor: استثناء متصل والمستثنى منه وقت محذوف والتقدير لا أخاف معبوداتكم في وقت من الأوقات

BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r1.claim: God’s complete knowledge explains the exception: He may decree harm to reach Abraham through them for some other reason, not through their power.
BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r1.anchor:
{وسع ربى كل شىء علما} كأنه تعليل
57
للاستثناء أي أحاط بكل شيء علما

BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r2.claim: Abraham calls them to reflect that lifeless idols cannot benefit or harm him.
BURSEVI:v3p45#3/r2.anchor: {أفلا تتذكرون} أي : أتعرضون عن التأمل في أن آلهتكم جمادات غير قادرة على شيء

QASHANI:6:80-86/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:80-86/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:80-86/r1.claim: Abraham's people dispute his denial of causal power in celestial bodies and created things and his refusal to worship anything besides God; after God's guidance he fears no alleged deity.
QASHANI:6:80-86/r1.anchor: في نفي التأثير عن الأجرام والأكون وترك تعبد كل ما سوى الله

QASHANI:6:80-86/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:80-86/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:80-86/r2.claim: Any harm from them occurs only if God wills it and comes from Him, not them; God knows Abraham's state and what benefits him.
QASHANI:6:80-86/r2.anchor: من جهتها بي من مكروه أو ضر يلحقني من جهتها وذلك منه وبعلمه لا منها

NAHHAS:v2p76/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p76/r12.speaker: نافع
NAHHAS:v2p76/r12.claim: Nafiʿ reads أتحاجوني with a light nūn; Abu Amr calls it incorrect, but Sibawayh permits it as relief from doubling.
NAHHAS:v2p76/r12.anchor: قرأ نافع ( أتحاجوني ) بنون مخففة وحكي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء أنه قال هو لحن

NAHHAS:v2p76/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p76/r13.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v2p76/r13.claim: Sibawayh permits the light nūn and cites a poem ending فليني as evidence for avoiding the doubled form.
NAHHAS:v2p76/r13.anchor: وأجاز سيبويه ذلك وقال استثقلوا التضعيف وأنشد ( تراه كالثغام يعل مسكا … يسوء الفاليات إذا فليني

NAHHAS:v2p76/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p76/r14.speaker: أبو عبيدة
NAHHAS:v2p76/r14.claim: Abu Ubayda says those who dislike the heavy form avoid two adjacent sukūns, wāw and nūn, by dropping one.
NAHHAS:v2p76/r14.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة وإنما كره التثقيل من كرهه للجمع بين ساكنين وهما الواو والنون

NAHHAS:v2p76/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p76/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p76/r15.claim: Al-Nahhas sides with Sibawayh: two sukūns are acceptable when the first is a long vowel and the second assimilated.
NAHHAS:v2p76/r15.anchor: قال أبو جعفر والقول في هذا قول سيبويه ولا ينكر الجمع بين ساكنين إذا كان الأول حرف مد

NAHHAS:v2p76/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p76/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p76/r16.claim: In وقد هدان, the yāʾ may be dropped because kasra indicates it and nūn compensates; retaining the yāʾ is also sound.
NAHHAS:v2p76/r16.anchor: بحذف الياء لأن الكسرة تدل عليها والنون عوض منها إذا حذفتها وإثباتها حسن

NAHHAS:v2p76/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p76/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p76/r17.claim: The phrase says Abraham fears the idols because they neither benefit nor harm; ما is accusative, and the exception is disconnected.
NAHHAS:v2p76/r17.anchor: ولا أخاف ما تشركون به ) أي لأنه لا ينفع ولا يضر و ( ما ) في موضع نصب

NAHHAS:v2p76/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p76/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p76/r18.claim: علما explains or specifies وسع ربي كل شيء.
NAHHAS:v2p76/r18.anchor: وسع ربي كل شيء علما ) بيان

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331/r1.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331/r1.anchor: عن الربيع : اما قوله : وحاجة قومه ، يقول : خاصموه .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331/r2.claim: To dispute with Abraham about God means to quarrel with him over God.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس : اتحاجوني في الله قال اتخاصموني في الله .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331/r3.claim: His people asked him to describe God and claimed their gods were better; Abraham answered that God had guided him.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق : وحاجة قومه عند ذلك في الله يستوصفونه اياه ، ويخبرونه ان الهتهم خير مما يعبد ، فقال : اتحاجوني في الله وقد هدان .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331/r4.speaker: كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331/r4.claim: God's knowledge in the Mother Book encompasses what He will create and what they will do.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1331/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس انه سال كعبا ، عن أم الكتاب ، فقال : ان الله علم ما هو خالق وما خلقه عاملون .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r3.claim: O my people begins Abraham's address to his people after the truth became clear, when he openly announced his opposition to them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r3.anchor: هو ابتداء خطابه لقومه بعد أن ظهر الحق له فأعلن بمخالفته قومه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r4.claim: The report that his people disputed with him is coordinated to his declaration in 6:79; waw makes it a self-contained report although its sequence is understood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r4.anchor: فجملة { وحاجة } عطف على جملة { إني وجهت وجهي للذي فطر السماوات والأرض }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r5.claim: Muhajja is a reciprocal form from hujja; it can describe genuine debate, or one-sided argument as reciprocal because the opponent must receive and answer it, or as an intensive form; the author prefers genuine exchange.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r5.anchor: والمحاجة مفاعلة متصرفة من الحجة ، وهي الدليل المؤيد للدعوى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r6.speaker: ابن عرفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r6.claim: Ibn Arafah says reciprocal morphology makes the grammatical subject the initiator; he explains 2:258 by Abraham starting the conversation and Nimrod starting the debate, but the author says grammarians do not establish that rule.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r6.anchor: وذكر الشيخ ابن عرفة في درس تفسيره : أن صيغة المفاعلة تقتضي أن المجعول فيها فاعلا هو البادىء بالمحاجة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r7.claim: Alternatively, the people may have argued for their religion while Abraham listened, with his listening treated as a response; their argument is omitted because the point is his steadfastness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p325/r7.anchor: وأبهم احتجاجهم هنا إذ لا يتعلق به غرض لأن الغرض هو الاعتبار بثبات إبراهيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r1.claim: The Quran elsewhere records their arguments: inherited worship of statues, whether idols hear or can help, and their attempt to burn Abraham; these were actual debates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r1.anchor: وقد ذكرت حججهم في مواضع في القرآن ، منها قوله في سورة الأنبياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r2.claim: Threatening Abraham with harm from their idols was not proof but something they regarded as proof, and it is included in the dispute described here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r2.anchor: ويدخل في المحاجة ما ليس بحجة ولكنه مما يرونه حججا بأن خوفوه غضب آلهتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r3.claim: His question, do you dispute with me about God, answers their challenge; if muhajja is reciprocal it closes debate, and if it means argument it is a reply, as in 3:20.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r3.anchor: وجملة { قال أتحاجوني في الله } جواب محاجتهم ، ولذلك فصلت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r4.claim: The interrogative rebukes them and gives up any hope of their returning to his belief; fi means about God's attributes and oneness, not about His person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r4.anchor: والاستفهام إنكار عليهم وتأييس من رجوعه إلى معتقدهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r5.claim: Wa-qad hadani is a circumstantial clause reinforcing the rebuke: there is no point disputing after God has guided Abraham, a fact they knew or were treated as knowing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p326/r5.anchor: أي لا جدوى لمحاجتكم إياي بعد أن هداني الله إلى الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r1.claim: Nafi, Ibn Amir, and Abu Jafar read a-taḥajjūni with one light n; al-Farisi says the second, protective n was deleted, while Sibawayh says the first, inflectional n was deleted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع ، وابن عامر ، وأبو جعفر { أتحاجوني } بنون واحدة خفيفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r2.claim: The remaining readers geminate n by assimilating the inflectional n into the protective n, lengthening the waw to separate the resulting consonants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r2.anchor: وقرأه البقية بتشديد النون لإدغام نون الرفع في نون الوقاية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r3.claim: Abu Amr is reported to call the one-n reading incorrect; Ibn Ashur says he would be mistaken, or the attribution would be mistaken, if this report is sound.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r3.anchor: وعن أبي عمرو بن العلاء : أن هذه القراءة لحن ، فإن صح ذلك عنه فهو مخطىء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r4.claim: Nafi's Qalun reading omits the speaker's ya in hadani both in pause and connection; some of the Ten omit it only in pause, as at 2:186.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p327/r4.anchor: وحذفت ياء المتكلم في قوله { وقد هدان } للتخفيف وصلا ووقفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328/r1.claim: No fear of their idols may coordinate with the dispute clause as a report, or with God's guidance as added rebuke; the latter is clearer because they already know he fears no idols.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328/r1.anchor: لأن عدم خوفه من آلهتهم قد ظهرت دلائله عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328/r2.claim: The wording implies they threatened him with their gods' harm, since otherwise denying fear would not relate to the challenge or to God's guidance; compare the threat against Hud.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328/r2.anchor: وتأكيد الإنكار بها أظهر منه لقوله { وقد هدان } لأن عدم خوفه من آلهتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328/r3.claim: Ma in what you associate with God refers to their deities; the attached pronoun may refer to God, making ba mark the verb's object, or to the relative ma, making ba causal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328/r3.anchor: يجوز أن يكون عائدا على اسم الجلالة فتكون الباء لتعدية فعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطية والطبري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r1.claim: They take the exception as disconnected, meaning but I fear something my Lord wills; the author prefers this since it clarifies that Abraham fears God's will, not idols, and rebukes his people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r1.anchor: وقد جعله ابن عطية استثناء منقطعا بمعنى لكن . وهو ظاهر كلام الطبري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري ومتابعوه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r2.claim: They treat the exception as connected, with an omitted set of times: Abraham fears harm only at a time when God wills something that idols may do through His power.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r2.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري ومتابعوه الاستثناء متصلا مفرغا عن مستثنى منه محذوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows the omitted set to be general circumstances: except when God wills something that Abraham fears from them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r3.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون المستثنى منه أحوالا عامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r4.claim: The statement that God encompasses all things in knowledge answers an implicit doubt: a servant who supports God's religion may still fear whatever harm God wisely wills.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r4.anchor: وهذا مقام أدب مع الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r5.claim: Do you not remember is coordinated to Abraham's denial of their argument; it rebukes failure to recall the idols' unfitness and the true God's attributes shown by His creation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p328#2/r5.anchor: والاستفهام إنكار لعدم تذكرهم مع وضوح دلائل التذكر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p314/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p314/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p314/r5.claim: Ḥājjahu derives from argument or proof; Ibrahim asks whether they are disputing with him about God’s unity.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p314/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p314/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p314/r6.claim: The readings retain both nūns, assimilate the first into the second, or delete one; Nafiʿ and Ibn ʿAmir delete the second because the first marks inflection, as Abu ʿAli explains with a poetic parallel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p314/r6.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «أتحاجونني» بإظهار النونين وهو الأصل، وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p314/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p314/r7.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p314/r7.claim: Abu ʿAli says the first nūn cannot be deleted because it marks inflection; the second is a preparatory marker before the speaker’s yāʾ, and the remaining nūn takes kasra by adjacency.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p314/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي: لا يجوز أن تحذف الأولى لأنها للإعراب وإنما حذفت الثانية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p314/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p314/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p314/r8.claim: Qad hadānī means God guided Ibrahim to knowledge and unity; the author says the Kisāʾī imāla is apt because the word’s root ends in yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p314/r8.anchor: و «قد هداني» أي أرشدني إلى معرفته وتوحيده، وأمال الكسائي «هدان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r1.claim: The people warned Ibrahim that their idols might afflict him with leprosy or disease for offending them; he says he fears them not because they have no power or benefit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r1.anchor: وحكي أن الكفار قالوا لإبراهيم عليه السلام خف أن تصيبك آلهتنا ببرص أو داء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r2.claim: Mā is a relative pronoun; the pronoun in bihi may refer to God, meaning idols you associate with Him, or to mā itself, meaning that by which you associate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r2.anchor: وما في هذا الموضع بمعنى الذي، والضمير في به يحتمل أن يعود على الله عز وجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r3.claim: The exception is disconnected: Ibrahim denies fearing them but allows that his Lord may will some harm; shayʾ is the object of wills.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r3.anchor: إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا استثناء ليس من الأول وشيئا منصوب ب يشاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r4.claim: ʿIlman is an accusative specification, a verbal noun used with agent meaning; the sense is that the Lord’s knowledge encompasses everything.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r4.anchor: وعلما نصب على التمييز وهو مصدر بمعنى الفاعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r5.claim: Afalā tathakkarūn is a rebuke that draws attention to their failure to reflect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315/r5.anchor: أفلا تتذكرون توقيف وتنبيه وإظهار لموضع التقصير منهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Abraham’s people argued with him about their gods and threatened him through them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi double the nūn in atuḥājjūnī and taʾmurūnī; Nafiʿ and Ibn ʿAmir lighten it by dropping the second nūn where the two meet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r3.claim: “Do you argue with me about God?” means about His oneness; “He guided me” means He showed him the way of guidance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r3.anchor: ﴿ أتحاجوني في الله ﴾ أي في توحيده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r4.speaker: الكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r4.claim: Al-Kisaʾi reads hadān with imāla of the dāl, appropriate to a verb whose root contains yāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي هداني بإمالة الدال والإمالة حسنة فيما كان أصله الياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r5.claim: Abraham does not fear the idols because they can neither harm nor benefit; he fears only what his Lord wills, whose knowledge encompasses everything fully.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p76#2/r5.anchor: لا أخافها لأنها لا تضر ولا تنفع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r1.claim: Abraham's people argued about monotheism with sophistry, but he asks how they can dispute after God opened his sight and guided him to the truth; their false claims deserve no attention.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى: وجادله قومه فيما ذهب إليه من التوحيد، وناظروه بشبه من القول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r2.claim: Abraham's refusal to fear their gods proves their claims false: if the idols can act, let them plot and hasten their harm.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r2.anchor: فإن كان لها صنع، فكيدوني بها [جميعا] (1) ولا تنظرون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r3.claim: The exception about God's will is disconnected: nothing harms or benefits except God alone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r3.anchor: وقوله: {إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا} استثناء منقطع. أي لا يضر ولا ينفع إلا الله، عز وجل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r4.claim: God's knowledge encompasses every thing, and no hidden matter escapes Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293/r4.anchor: {وسع ربي كل شيء علما} أي: أحاط علمه بجميع الأشياء، فلا تخفى (2) عليه خافية.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r1.claim: The call to remember means considering Abraham's explanation, recognizing the idols' falsehood, and abandoning their worship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r1.anchor: {أفلا تتذكرون} أي: فيما بينته (3) لكم فتعتبرون أن هذه الآلهة باطلة، فتزجروا (4) عن عبادتها؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r2.claim: Abraham's argument parallels Hud's challenge to Aad: he disavowed their idols and challenged them to plot against him while trusting God, as narrated in Hud.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p293#2/r2.anchor: وهذه الحجة نظير ما احتج به نبي الله هود، عليه السلام، على قومه عاد، فيما قص عنهم

JISHUMI:v3p2303/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r1.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r1.claim: These readers lighten the nūn in a-taḥājjūnī by deleting one of two nūns; other readers assimilate them and read a doubled nūn.
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر وأبو جعفر: أتحاجوني خفيفة النون على حذف إحدى النونين

JISHUMI:v3p2303/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r2.claim: They retain the yāʾ in هداني, while other readers omit it for ease because context supplies it.
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: هداني بإثبات الياء على الأصل

JISHUMI:v3p2303/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r3.claim: Muḥājja is each disputant's demand for proof and presentation of evidence; guidance is direction leading to truth, and sulṭān means proof or power enabling control.
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r3.anchor: المحاجة: طلب كل واحد من الخصمين الحجة، وإيراد كل واحد الحجة على صاحبه.

JISHUMI:v3p2303/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r5.claim: The exception in ‘unless my Lord wills’ may be disconnected, meaning ‘but I fear my Lord's reproach,’ or literal: idols could be given power or restored by God's will.
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r5.anchor: قيل: نصب على تقدير: لكن أخاف مسبة ربي، و(إلا) ههنا بمعنى: (لكن)

JISHUMI:v3p2303/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r6.claim: Abraham's ‘how should I fear?’ is a denial: powerless idols cannot benefit or harm, and the question challenges people for fearing them while worshipping without proof.
JISHUMI:v3p2303/r6.anchor: والمراد الإنكار؛ أي لا ينبغي أن أخاف ما لا ينفع ولا يضر.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r1.claim: Abraham’s people disputed monotheism; ‘God guided me’ means He guided him to affirm divine oneness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r1.anchor: وكانوا حاجوه في توحيد الله ونفي الشركاء عنه منكرين لذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r2.claim: They warned idols could harm Abraham. He fears them only if God wills harm, perhaps for a sin or by enabling the idols; God knows all.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r2.anchor: وقد خوفوه أن معبوداتهم تصيبه بسوء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r3.claim: The appeal asks them to distinguish sound from false and the capable from the powerless.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r3.anchor: فتميزوا بين الصحيح والفاسد والقادر والعاجز

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r4.claim: Abraham contrasts fearing powerless idols with their failure to fear associating God with beings unsupported by proof.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r4.anchor: وما لكم تنكرون علي الأمن في موضع الأمن

MUQATIL:6:76-80/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:76-80/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:76-80/r3.claim: When Nimrod claimed to give life and death by killing one man and sparing another, Abraham challenged him to bring the sun from the west; Nimrod was confounded.
MUQATIL:6:76-80/r3.anchor: فعمد نمروذ إلى إنسان فقتله، وجاء بآخر فتركه،

MUQATIL:6:76-80/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:76-80/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:76-80/r4.claim: Abraham’s people feared their powerless idols would ruin or afflict him; he says they neither hear, see, benefit nor harm, and only fears God’s will, whose knowledge encompasses all.
MUQATIL:6:76-80/r4.anchor: وهى لا تسمع ولا تبصر شيئا، ولا تنفع ولا تضر، وتنحتونها بأيديكم،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r1.claim: Abraham's people argued against God's oneness and denied partners to Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r1.anchor: فى توحيد الله تعالى ونفى الشركاء عنه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r2.speaker: مدني
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r2.claim: The Medinan reading has اتحاجونى for the question about disputing Abraham over God.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ قال أتحاجوني في الله ﴾ فى توحيده اتحاجونى مدنى وابن ذكوان

NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r3.speaker: ابن ذكوان
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r3.claim: Ibn Dhakwān shares the reading اتحاجونى.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r3.anchor: والياء فى الوصل أبو عمرو ولما خوفوه أن معبوداتهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr retains the yāʾ in وقد هدان when pausing or connecting the reading.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r4.anchor: والياء فى الوصل أبو عمرو ولما خوفوه أن معبوداتهم تصيبه بسوء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r5.claim: Abraham says he never fears their idols, which have no power to benefit or harm; only God could choose to make something harmful or beneficial.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r5.anchor: لا أخاف معبوداتكم فى وقت قط لانها لا تقدر على منفعة ولا مضرة إلا إذا شاء ربى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r6.claim: God knows everything, so no harm or benefit reaches anyone except by His knowledge.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r6.anchor: فلا يصيب عبدا شيء من ضر أو نفع إلا بعلمه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r7.claim: Remembering should lead them to distinguish the powerful God from powerless idols.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#2/r7.anchor: ﴿ أفلا تتذكرون ﴾ فتميزوا بين القادر والعاجز

SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r1.claim: Nafi, Ibn Dhakwan, and sometimes Hisham read a light nūn in atuḥājjūnī; the rest read it doubled, the original form from nūn of indicative inflection plus protective nūn.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r1.anchor: والباقون بنون ثقيلة، والتثقيل هو الأصل

SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r2.claim: The two nūns have four treatments: separation, retention, assimilation, or deletion; Qurʾanic examples display all four across the cited passages.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r2.anchor: وفيها لغات ثلاث: الفك وتركهما على حالهما، والإدغام، والحذف،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r3.claim: In the other cited forms, Nafi deletes a nūn across the examples, Ibn Kathir assimilates at 39:64, and Hisham assimilates in 46:17 while others pronounce distinctly.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r3.anchor: فإنه/ يقرأ في الزمر أيضا بحذف إحداهما، وقوله تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r4.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r4.claim: Sibawayh and his followers say the first nūn, the inflectional one, is deleted; al-Akhfash and his followers say the second, protective one.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r4.anchor: واختلف النحاة في أيتهما المحذوفة: فمذهب سيبويه ومن تبعه أن المحذوفة هي الأولى، ومذهب الأخفش ومن تبعه أن المحذوفة هي الثانية،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r5.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r5.claim: Sibawayh argues that the inflectional nūn is independently known to drop; his poem retains the future sense after a required fāʾ, so the deletion is poetic rather than jussive.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r5.anchor: استدل سيبويه على ذلك بأن نون الرفع قد عهد حذفها دون ملاقاة مثل رفعا

SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r6.claim: The line ‘you stay and she stays rubbing’ also implies deletion of the indicative nūn, and the hadith has a negative rather than prohibitive lā before ‘enter’ and ‘believe.’
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث: " والذي نفسي بيده لا تدخلوا الجنة حتى تؤمنوا ولا تؤمنوا حتى تحابوا "

SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r7.claim: Because a ḍamma may be omitted in eloquent forms, its substitute nūn may likewise be omitted; Abu Amr’s recited forms and a poem illustrate this.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80/r7.anchor: وأيضا فإن النون نائبة عن الضمة، والضمة قد عهد حذفها في فصيح الكلام كقراءة أبي عمرو:

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r1.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r1.claim: Sibawayh argues that if the inflectional ending itself is sometimes dropped, its substitute nūn can be dropped too; a critic answers that a root may be deletable while its derivative is not.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r1.anchor: وإذا ثبت حذف الأصل فليثبت حذف الفرع لئلا يلزم تفضيل فرع على أصله

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r2.claim: A further objection says deleting the protective nūn would leave the inflectional nūn to be deleted under a jussive or subjunctive, while deleting the inflectional nūn avoids a second deletion.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r2.anchor: وذلك أنه لو كان المحذوف نون الرفع لأجل نون الوقاية ودخل الجازم والناصب

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r3.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r3.claim: Sibawayh notes that the protective nūn is already kasra, so retaining it avoids changing the indicative nūn from fatḥa to kasra; he also cites poetry with a deleted nūn before nā.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r3.anchor: واستدلوا لسيبويه أيضا بأن نون الوقاية مكسورة، فبقاؤها على حالها لا يلزم منه تغيير

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r4.claim: The counterargument says the inflectional nūn itself marks case and therefore also has a strong claim against deletion.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r4.anchor: وعورض هذا بأن نون الرفع أيضا لها قوة لدلالتها على الإعراب

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r5.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r5.claim: Sibawayh analyzes the deleted nūn in the cited ‘they dislike you’ poem as the subject nūn, not the protective nūn.

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r6.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash argues that the second nūn causes the heaviness, is redundant, and may be dropped because the first nūn already receives the kasra it was meant to protect.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r6.anchor: واستدل الأخفش بأن الثقل إنما حصل بالثانية، ولأنه قد استغني عنها،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r7.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash also points to the loss of the protective nūn in laytani, pronounced laytī, with a poetic example.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#2/r7.anchor: وأيضا فإنها تحذف في نحو: ليتني فيقال: ليتي،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r1.claim: Deleting one nūn in this construction is fluent, accepted Arabic, not limited to poetic necessity; the attributed objections are false given its canonical transmission and Ghatafan usage.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r1.anchor: واعلم أن حذف النون في هذا النحو جائز فصيح، ولا يلتفت إلى قول من منع ذلك إلا في ضرورة

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r2.speaker: مكي ابن أبي طالب
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r2.claim: Makki calls the deletion distant, ugly, and permissible only in poetry, arguing that the Qurʾan has no need for it.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r2.anchor: قال: " الحذف بعيد في العربية قبيح مكروه، وإنما يجوز في الشعر للوزن،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r3.claim: The author rejects claims that the light-nūn reading is a solecism because it is mutawātir and attested Arabic.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r3.anchor: وهذان القولان مردودان عليهما لتواتر ذلك، وقد قدمت الدليل على صحته لغة،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r4.claim: Fī Allāh attaches to atuḥājjūnī rather than ḥājjahu; the author questions this coordination analysis because the quoted clause seems separate and means ‘about God and His oneness.’
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r4.anchor: و " في الله " متعلق ب " أتحاجوني " لا ب " حاجه " ، والمسألة من باب التنازع،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r5.claim: The Shaykh says the second verb governs under coordination because the first is pronominalized and would require an omitted complement if it governed.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r5.anchor: وأعمل الثاني لأنه لما أضمر في الأول حذف، ولو أعمل الأول لأضمر في الثاني من غير حذف،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r6.claim: The author objects that the meaning does not appear to make ‘he disputed’ govern ‘about God’; the quoted speech is more naturally a new clause.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r6.anchor: وفيه نظر، من حيث/ إن المعنى ليس على تسلط " وحاجه " على قوله " في الله "؛

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r7.claim: ‘While He has guided me’ is most naturally circumstantial from the first-person pronoun in ‘do you dispute with me?’
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r7.anchor: وقد هداني " في محل نصب على الحال، وفي صاحبها وجهان أظهرهما: أنه التاء في " أتحاجونني "

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r8.claim: Alternatively, the clause is circumstantial from God: they dispute while He is guiding Abraham, so their case is futile.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#3/r8.anchor: والثاني: أنه حال من " الله " أي: أتخاصمونني فيه حال كونه هاديا لي،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r1.claim: ‘I do not fear what you associate’ may be an independent statement of confidence in God; his people had threatened him for insulting their idols.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r1.anchor: أخبر عليه السلام بأنه لا يخاف ما تشركون به ربه ثقة به، وكانوا قد خوفوه من ضرر يحصل له

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r2.claim: Alternatively it is circumstantial: either a second circumstance of the speaker in ‘do you dispute,’ or a nested circumstance of ‘He guided me,’ requiring an implied subject before the present verb after wāw.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون في محل نصب على الحال باعتبارين أحدهما: أن تكون ثانية عطفا على الأولى،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r3.claim: Mā may be a verbal noun, relative pronoun, or indefinite description; if verbal, bihā refers to God and the sense is ‘I fear no associating partners with God,’ with an omitted object.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r3.anchor: و " ما " يجوز فيها الأوجه الثلاثة: أن تكون مصدرية، وعلى هذا فالهاء في " به " لا تعود على " ما " عند الجمهور، بل تعود على الله تعالى،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r4.claim: If mā is relative or indefinite descriptive, bihā refers back to it and means ‘what you associate with God’; the object is again omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r4.anchor: وأن تكون بمعنى الذي، وأن تكون نكرة موصوفة، والهاء في " به " على هذين الوجهين تعود على " ما " ،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa suggests an implied ‘cause’ before the pronoun, but the author says this addition is unnecessary.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r5.anchor: وقدر أبو البقاء قبل الضمير مضافا فقال: " ويجوز أن تكون الهاء عائدة على " ما " أي: ولا أخاف الذي تشركون بسببه "

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r6.claim: The exception ‘unless my Lord wills something’ is most likely connected, though a disconnected exception is also reported.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r6.anchor: قوله: " إلا أن يشاء " في هذا الاستثناء قولان، أظهرهما: أنه متصل، والثاني: أنه منقطع،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari makes the connected exception temporal: Abraham fears no powerless idols at any time unless God wills something fearsome.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r7.anchor: فجعله الزمخشري زمانا فقال: " إلا وقت مشيئة ربي شيئا يخاف،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqa instead makes the connected exception circumstantial: he fears them in every state except the state of God’s willing.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r8.anchor: وجعله أبو البقاء حالا فقال: تقديره إلا في حال مشيئة ربي

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya, al-Hawfi, and one view of Abu al-Baqa take the exception as disconnected: Abraham fears God’s will to afflict him.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#4/r9.anchor: وممن ذهب إلى انقطاعه ابن عطية والحوفي وأبو البقاء في أحد الوجهين

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r1.claim: Shayʾan is most likely a cognate accusative, ‘a willing of some sort’; the alternative is a direct object of ‘wills.’
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r1.anchor: أظهرهما: أنه منصوب على المصدر تقديره: إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا من المشيئة،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r2.claim: The cognate accusative is preferred because repetition for emphasis strengthens the meaning, and objects of ‘will’ are named when unusual.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r2.anchor: وإنما كان الأول أظهر لوجهين، أحدهما: أن الكلام المؤكد أقوى وأثبت في النفس من غير المؤكد.

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r3.claim: The cited poetic line illustrates naming the object of a wish when it is remarkable.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنه قد تقدم أن مفعول المشيئة والإرادة لا يذكران إلا إذا كان فيهما غرابة كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r4.claim: ʿIlman is most likely specification transformed from the subject: ‘my Lord’s knowledge encompasses everything,’ as in 19:4.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r4.anchor: أظهرهما: أنه منصوب على التمييز، وهو محول عن الفاعل تقديره: وسع علم ربي كل شيء،

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa treats ʿilman as an absolute object because encompassing entails knowing; the author calls his metaphor remote.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r5.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " لأن ما يسع الشيء فقد أحاط به، والعالم بالشيء محيط بعلمه "

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r6.claim: On either analysis, ‘everything’ is the object of wasiʿa.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r6.anchor: و " كل شيء " مفعول لوسع على كلا التقديرين.

SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r7.claim: ‘Will you not remember?’ is an independent sentence of admonition and reproach, so it has no syntactic position.
SAMIN-DURR:6:80#5/r7.anchor: و " أفلا تتذكرون " جملة تقرير وتوبيخ، ولا محل لها لاستئنافها.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:80/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80/r1.speaker: نافع
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80/r1.claim: Nafi' reads the n in a-tuhajjooni with light pronunciation; the other readers double it, though a variant is reported from Ibn Amir through Hisham.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع بتخفيف النون، وشدد النون الباقون

QURTUBI-FULL:6:80/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80/r2.claim: The doubled form contracts two original nuns, the nominative marker and a separator before ya; the light form drops the second nun to avoid duplication while retaining the grammatical marker.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80/r2.anchor: الأصل فيه نونان، الأولى علامة الرفع والثانية فاصلة بين الفعل والياء

QURTUBI-FULL:6:80/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80/r3.claim: Abu Amr calls the light reading ungrammatical, but Sibawayh permits it because doubled consonants are burdensome and cites a line of poetry.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80/r3.anchor: وحكي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء أن هذه القراءة لحن. وأجاز سيبويه ذلك فقال: استثقلوا التضعيف

QURTUBI-FULL:6:80#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80#2/r1.claim: Abraham does not fear the idols because they cannot benefit or harm him, despite his people threatening him with their many gods; harm could occur only if God willed it for a sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80#2/r1.anchor: ولا أخاف ما تشركون به } أي لأنه لا ينفع ولا يضر وكانوا خوفوه بكثرة آلهتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:80#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80#2/r2.claim: The exception is not from the preceding fear: God may decree some hardship for a sin; the pronoun in bihi may refer either to God or to the idol.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80#2/r2.anchor: وهذا استثناء ليس من الأول. والهاء في «به» يحتمل أن تكون لله عز وجل، ويجوز أن تكون للمعبود

QURTUBI-FULL:6:80#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80#2/r3.claim: Abraham's phrase also means that God does not will him to fear the idols; God's knowledge encompasses everything.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:80#2/r3.anchor: يعني أن الله تعالى لا يشاء أن أخافهم. ثم قال: { وسع ربي كل شيء علما

RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r1.claim: Abraham’s people first appealed to ancestral imitation and rejected the notion of one God, as in 43:23 and 38:5; they also threatened that their idols would afflict him, like Hūd’s people in 11:54.
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r1.anchor: أوردوا عليه حججا على صحة أقوالهم

RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r2.claim: Abraham answers that sound proof has given him guidance, so their defective arguments and false words deserve no consideration.
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r2.anchor: يعني لما ثبت بالدليل الموجب للهداية واليقين صحة قولي ، فكيف يلتفت

RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r3.claim: He rejects fear of idols because fear properly concerns an agent able to cause benefit or harm, while idols are inert and powerless.
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r3.anchor: والأصنام جمادات لا تقدر ولا قدرة لها على النفع والضر

RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r4.claim: Even if talismans appear to have effects, their effects come from the stars, whose powers God created; ultimate fear and hope therefore belong to God.
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r4.anchor: وقد دللنا على أن قوى الكواكب على التأثيرات إنما يحصل من خلق الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r5.claim: The exception except if my Lord wills may mean that Abraham sins and is punished, faces worldly trials and loss of some accustomed blessings, or that God revives and empowers the idols; the wording can bear all three.
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r5.anchor: واللفظ يحتمل كل هذه الوجوه ، وحاصل الأمر أنه لا يبعد

RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r6.claim: Abraham anticipates future misfortunes so foolish people will not mistake them for punishment caused by his rejection of idols.
RAZI-FULL:v13p48/r6.anchor: ذكر إبراهيم عليه السلام ذلك حتى لو أنه حدث به شيء من المكاره لم يحمل على هذا السبب

RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r1.claim: God encompasses all knowledge and acts only with wisdom and benefit; any worldly hardship would reflect what God knows best, not punishment for challenging the idols.
RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r1.anchor: { وسع ربى كل شىء علما } يعني أنه علام الغيوب

RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r2.claim: People should recognize that denying partners to God and affirming monotheism do not bring punishment or make one deserve it.
RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r2.anchor: نفي الشركاء والأضداد والأنداد عن الله تعالى لا يوجب حلول العقاب

RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r3.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r3.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read ataḥājjūnī with a light nūn by deleting one of the two; other readers retain the doubled nūn through assimilation.
RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r3.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر { أتحاجونى } خفيفة النون على حذف أحد النونين

RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r4.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir retain the yāʾ in hadānī, while the other readers omit it for ease of pronunciation.
RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r4.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر { هدانى } بإثبات الياء على الأصل والباقون بحذفها للتخفيف

RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r5.claim: Debate over God merits praise when it establishes true religion, as Abraham’s argument does (6:83), and blame when it establishes falsehood; Qur’anic and hadith censure of disputation concerns false doctrine.
RAZI-FULL:v13p49/r5.anchor: ولا فرق بين هذين البابين إلا أن المحاجة في تقرير الدين الحق توجب أعظم أنواح المدح والثناء

STUDYQURAN:6:74/r50.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r50.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r50.claim: Abraham's people disputed by appealing to ancestral custom, objecting to worship of one God, or threatening harm from their idols.
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r50.anchor: their false deities and idols would bring harm upon him for his rejection of them (R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:6:74/r51.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r51.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r51.claim: Abraham asks how vain arguments could affect someone guided by God and notes that idols can bring neither harm nor benefit.
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r51.anchor: one, such as himself, who has been guided by God, and how they can hope to frighten him by invoking the partners

STUDYQURAN:6:74/r52.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r52.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r52.claim: Abraham fears only what comes from God; fearing the alleged partners would only occur if God willed to test him.
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r52.anchor: he fears only what comes from God, and if he were to fear the partners his people ascribe to Him, it would only be as a result of God’s Will to test him in some way (R)

STUDYQURAN:6:74/r53.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r53.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r53.claim: God's encompassing Knowledge means all things occur according to His Wisdom and Knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r53.anchor: everything occurs according to His Wisdom (R) and Knowledge

TAB-FULL:v9p365/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r1.claim: Abraham's people argue that their idols are better than his God; Abraham says he was guided to know God's unity and worship Him alone.
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r1.anchor: التي يعبدونها خير من إلهه. {قال} [البقرة: 30] إبراهيم: {أتحاجوني في الله} [الأنعام: 80] يقول: أتجادلونني في توحيدي الله

TAB-FULL:v9p365/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r2.claim: They threaten that their idols may afflict him with leprosy or insanity, but Abraham does not fear powerless idols; only God can harm him if He wills.
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r2.anchor: وذلك أنهم قالوا له: إنا نخاف أن تمسك آلهتنا بسوء من برص أو خبل

TAB-FULL:v9p365/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r3.claim: He says the people invoked other gods alongside God and threatened Abraham with insanity from their idols.
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج: {وحاجه قومه قال أتحاجوني في الله وقد هدان} [الأنعام: 80] قال: دعا قومه مع الله آلهة

TAB-FULL:v9p365/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r4.claim: God encompasses all knowledge because He created everything; idols cannot harm, benefit, or understand anything.
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r4.anchor: وعلم ربي كل شيء فلا يخفى عليه شيء، لأنه خالق كل شيء، وليس كالآلهة التي لا تضر ولا تنفع

TAB-FULL:v9p365/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r5.claim: The idols are carved wood and images, powerless and without understanding, unlike the Creator who holds all power and good.
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r5.anchor: وإنما هي خشبة منحوتة وصورة ممثلة

TAB-FULL:v9p365/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r6.claim: The closing question urges the ignorant to recognize the error of worshipping powerless images and abandoning the Creator of all things.
TAB-FULL:v9p365/r6.anchor: أفلا تعتبرون أيها الجهلة، فتعقلوا خطأ ما أنتم عليه مقيمون من عبادتكم صورة مصورة وخشبة منحوتة

ZAJJAJ:v2p267/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p267/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p267/r7.claim: Abraham’s people argued about God by worshipping stars, sun, moon, and idols; ‘in God’ means about His oneness, which He had made clear to Abraham.
ZAJJAJ:v2p267/r7.anchor:
ومحاجتهم إياه كانت - والله أعلم - فيما عبدوا مع الله عز وجل من
الكواكب والشمس والقمر والأصنام،

ZAJJAJ:v2p267/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p267/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p267/r8.claim: The objects they associate with God can neither harm nor benefit; Abraham fears only if God wills to punish him for a sin, and أن is accusative as a noun.
ZAJJAJ:v2p267/r8.anchor:
أي هذه الأشياء التي تعبدونها لا تضر ولا تنفع، ولا أخافها.
(إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا).
إلا أن يشاء أن يعذبني بذنب

TABATABAI:6:80/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80/r1.claim: The people appeal to fear of divine anger and punishment, the stronger motive for worship; hope for blessings has less force because people attribute material fortune to effort, inheritance, or luck.
TABATABAI:6:80/r1.anchor: الذي بعثهم إلى اتخاذ الآلهة وعبادتها أحد أمرين الخوف من سخطها

TABATABAI:6:80/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80/r2.claim: The Qur'an correspondingly emphasizes warning more than glad tidings, although both are prophetic methods and duties.
TABATABAI:6:80/r2.anchor: نرى أن القرآن يذكر الإنذار من وظائف الأنبياء أكثر من ذكر التبشير

TABATABAI:6:80/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80/r3.claim: Abraham's people use fear to dissuade him from Allah's lordship and urge him to accept their gods; his reply addresses both rejection of Allah and affirmation of their gods.
TABATABAI:6:80/r3.anchor: اختار قوم إبراهيم عليه السلام في محاجتهم إياه عندما كلموه في أمر الآلهة سبيل الخوف

TABATABAI:6:80/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80/r4.claim: The plain reading of “my Lord has guided me” is that Abraham has settled knowledge from God's showing him the kingdom of heaven and earth, so further inquiry is unnecessary.
TABATABAI:6:80/r4.anchor: إني واقع في أمر مفروغ عنه ومهتد بهداية ربي

TABATABAI:6:80#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80#2/r1.claim: More deeply, guidance itself proves God's lordship: guiding someone to the true Lord is an act of governance, and another being would not guide Abraham to reject its own divinity.
TABATABAI:6:80#2/r1.anchor: استدلال بنفس الهداية لا استغناء بالهداية عن الاستدلال وتقريره أن الله

TABATABAI:6:80#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80#2/r2.claim: Abraham's opponents could claim that one of their gods afflicted him and forced him away from their worship, as the people of Hud accused Hud of divine affliction.
TABATABAI:6:80#2/r2.anchor: نظير ما شافهت به عاد هودا عليه السلام لما دعاهم إلى توحيد الله

TABATABAI:6:80#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r1.claim: God made the realm in which the people live for sound and well-ordered purposes.
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r1.anchor: مملكته التي أوجدها لغايات صحيحة متقنة

TABATABAI:6:80#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r2.claim: God does not leave beneficial or harmful events within His realm unattended: He either prevents them or permits them.
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r2.anchor: لا يستقبله بأحد أمرين إما المنع أو الإذن

TABATABAI:6:80#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r3.claim: God's encompassing knowledge means no event occurs in His realm without His knowing and either preventing or permitting it; any hypothetical fear would therefore attest His lordship.
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r3.anchor: فهو يعلم كل ما يحدث ويجري من خير وشر في مملكته

TABATABAI:6:80#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r4.claim: The no-fear statement completes the guidance argument and also stands as a full proof against the partners; the exception is a concession, knowledge explains it, and the closing question appeals to innate reason.
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r4.anchor: فقوله { ولا أخاف ما تشركون به } كالمتمم للحجة

TABATABAI:6:80#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r5.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r5.claim: Most exegetes take Abraham's mention of guidance to mean he needs no further argument, though Tabatabai objects that the context presents an argument.
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r5.anchor: أورد أكثرهم فيه الوجه الأول من الوجهين اللذين قدمناهما

TABATABAI:6:80#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r6.claim: One interpretation makes the exception mean God could revive and empower the idols to benefit or harm, so their power would itself show they are created.
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r6.anchor: قيل معناه إلا أن يغلب ربي هذه الأصنام التي تخوفونني بها

TABATABAI:6:80#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r7.claim: That interpretation wrongly attributes benefit and harm to the partners, contrary to the Qur'anic teaching that only God possesses either.
TABATABAI:6:80#3/r7.anchor: تخالف التعليم الإلهي في كتابه فإن القرآن يصرح أن لا يملك نفعا ولا ضررا إلا الله

TABATABAI:6:80#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r1.claim: Reviving the idols would not answer pagans, who already accept that idols and their lords are created and dependent on God, even if some are timeless.
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r1.anchor: لا يضر أهل الأوثان فإنهم كما عرفت لا ينكرون كون الأصنام

TABATABAI:6:80#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes the exception from every kind of fear: Abraham fears any punishment or misfortune God wills, whether as recompense or without prior cause.
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r2.anchor: وقيل إن معنى الاستثناء إني لا اخاف شركائكم

TABATABAI:6:80#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r3.claim: Tabatabai calls this reading strained because it shifts from fear of the partners to all possible fears without support from the sentence.
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r3.anchor: ووجه التعسف في هذا المعنى لا يحتاج إلى بيان

TABATABAI:6:80#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r4.claim: Commentators say the statement about God's knowledge may praise Him, taunt the idols' ignorance, or explain that He knows hidden matters and acts only wisely.
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r4.anchor: إنه ثناء منه عليه السلام لربه بعد إتمام الحجة

TABATABAI:6:80#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r5.claim: The taunt would more naturally invoke God's power, while the explanation that He does only what is good should mention wisdom as well as knowledge.
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r5.anchor: فما وجه العدول عن القدرة إلى العلم

TABATABAI:6:80#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r6.claim: Some take God's knowledge as explaining the exception: He may already know He will allow harm, such as an idol falling on Abraham or the sun's heat injuring him.
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r6.anchor: وقيل إنه كالتعليل للاستثناء بجواز أن يكون قد سبق في علمه تعالى إصابته بسوء

TABATABAI:6:80#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r7.claim: Knowledge alone is not the most fitting explanation for harm; power or wisdom would better ground that claim.
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r7.anchor: التمسك بالقدرة أو الحكمة أنسب للتعليل من العلم

TABATABAI:6:80#4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r8.claim: A further interpretation says God's all-encompassing knowledge and will leave no creature able to affect His actions through intercession or other influence; it cites the throne verse.
TABATABAI:6:80#4/r8.anchor: علم ربي وسع كل شيء وأحاط به ومشيئته مرتبطة بعلمه المحيط

TABATABAI:6:80-81/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80-81/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80-81/r1.claim: The all-knowledge interpretation does not work by knowledge alone: it also needs unrestricted power and will, which the proposed explanation itself invokes.
TABATABAI:6:80-81/r1.anchor: هذا الوجه لا يتم بسعة العلم وحدها وإنما يتم بها وبإطلاق القدرة والمشيئة

TABATABAI:6:80-81/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:80-81/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:80-81/r2.claim: The cited intercession verses affirm causal mediation by God's permission; they do not deny intercession, and the Qur'an consistently recognizes causation.
TABATABAI:6:80-81/r2.anchor: الآيات المذكورة مسوقة لإثبات الشفاعة بمعنى التوسط في السببية بإذن من الله سبحانه

TABRISI:6:80-81/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:80-81/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:80-81/r1.claim: Medinan readers and Ibn ʿĀmir through Ibn Dhakwān lighten the nūn in “a-tuḥājjūnī”; the rest double it. The light form deletes the second nūn to avoid doubling, preserving the inflectional first nūn.
TABRISI:6:80-81/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة وابن عامر في رواية ابن ذكوان أتحاجوني خفيفة النون والباقون بالتشديد

TABRISI:6:80-81/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:80-81/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:6:80-81/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī argues that the second nūn is omitted in the light reading because repetition is heavy; deleting the first would remove inflection, and he cites analogous nūn deletion in speech and poetry.
TABRISI:6:80-81/r2.anchor: فأما وجه التخفيف فإنه حذفت النون الثانية لالتقاء النونين والتضعيف يكره

TABRISI:6:80-81/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:80-81/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:80-81/r3.claim: The exception in “unless my Lord wills something” is parsed as an independent exception meaning Abraham fears only God’s will; an alternative makes it connected, if God empowers the idols to harm or benefit.
TABRISI:6:80-81/r3.anchor: موضع أن يشاء نصب أي لا أخاف إلا مشيئة الله وهذا استثناء منقطع.

TABRISI:6:80-81/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:80-81/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:80-81/r4.claim: Abraham says God guided him to know and affirm divine unity; he does not fear idols, since a broken idol cannot defend itself and a setting star is created, so neither can harm or benefit.
TABRISI:6:80-81/r4.anchor: وفقني لمعرفته ولطف بي في العلم بتوحيده وترك الشرك وإخلاص العبادة له

TABRISI:6:80-81/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:80-81/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:80-81/r5.claim: One explanation of the exception is that if God gave the idols power to harm or benefit, this would itself prove they were created and God alone merits worship; the author calls this the stronger view.
TABRISI:6:80-81/r5.anchor: والأول أجود. ثم احتج ع عليهم وأكد الحجاج بقوله

TABRISI:6:80-81/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:80-81/r6.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:6:80-81/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan instead understands Abraham to fear only that God may punish him for some sin or independently will harm him.
TABRISI:6:80-81/r6.anchor: والثاني: قول الحسن معناه لا أخاف الأوثان إلا أن يشاء ربي

THALABI:v4p164/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p164/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p164/r7.claim: حاجه means his people argued with him; Ibrahim says God has guided him to monotheism and truth, so their debate cannot undo that guidance.
THALABI:v4p164/r7.anchor: وحاجه أي خاصمه قومه في دينه قال لهم أتحاجوني في الله وقد هدان عرفني التوحيد والحق

THALABI:v4p164/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p164/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p164/r8.claim: Ibrahim’s people warned that their idols might afflict him with leprosy or madness for insulting them; he says he fears them only if his Lord wills.
THALABI:v4p164/r8.anchor: وذلك إنهم قالوا له: أما تخاف أن تمسك آلهتنا بسوء من برص أو خبل

THALABI:v4p164/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p164/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p164/r9.claim: God’s knowledge encompasses everything, so Ibrahim asks whether the people will remember that the idols are subject to His will.
THALABI:v4p164/r9.anchor: وسع ربي كل شيء علما يعني أحاط علمه بكل شيء أفلا تتذكرون

ASAD-NOTES:6:80#n67/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:80#n67/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:80#n67/r1.claim: The phrase means “unless my Sustainer wills a thing.”
ASAD-NOTES:6:80#n67/r1.anchor: unless my Sustainer wills a thing

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r1.claim: Abraham’s people disputed with and argued against him about their gods, using them to frighten him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r1.anchor: خاصمه وجادله في آلهتهم وخوفوه بها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r2.claim: Their debate concerned stars, sun, moon, and idols; Abraham’s question rejects argument against God’s oneness after God had shown him guidance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r2.anchor: فيما عبدوا مع الله جل وعز من الكواكب والشمس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r3.claim: The interrogative is a rebuke denying that they can argue him away from the guidance he has received.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r3.anchor: وهذا الاستفهام معناه الإنكار للمحاجة في الصرف عن الهداية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r4.claim: The geminated nūn in tuḥājjūnnī joins two nūns by assimilation; Nāfiʿ reads a light nūn after deleting one, with the second deleted because it is heavier and the first marks inflection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r4.anchor: نافع مخففة النون حذف إحدى النونين تخفيفا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r5.speaker: عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r5.claim: A line attributed to ʿAmr illustrates deleting the second nūn that accompanies the yāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r5.anchor: قول عمرو: تراه كالثغام يعل مسكا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r6.claim: They warned Abraham that their gods could afflict him with madness, explaining his denial that he feared them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r6.anchor: خوفوه آلهتهم أن يصيبه منها خبل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r7.claim: The worshipped objects neither harm nor benefit; the exception means “but I fear my Lord’s will to punish me,” with an accusative clause and a disconnected exception.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r7.anchor: لا تضر (¬3) ولا تنفع ولا أخافها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r8.claim: The will, illnesses, and diseases are under God’s control, answering their warning that the idols might harm Abraham.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p251/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس (¬7): (يريد: أن المشيئة والأسقام والأمراض إليه)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:80-82/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:80-82/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:80-82/r1.claim: Abraham’s people argued against his abandoning idols and threatened that they would harm him; he answers that God guided him to worship and oneness, and he fears only God’s will.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:80-82/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:80-82/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:80-82/r2.claim: God’s knowledge encompasses everything completely; Abraham asks if they will take heed and abandon idols.

ELMALILI:6:75-82/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r13.claim: Abraham’s people challenge and threaten him, seeking to win the argument; he dismisses their verbal and practical dispute and intimidation, then argues from love and fear to establish lordship and worship.
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r13.anchor: Kavmi de kendisine karşı mücadele ve tahvif ile hüccet yarışına kalkıştılar, galebe fikrine düştüler.

ELMALILI:6:75-82/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:75-82/r14.claim: Abraham begins his reply by asking whether they dispute with him about God when He has already guided him.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r1.claim: Abraham's people debate him and offer arguments against the clear reasoning from natural signs for God's unity; their arguments are omitted to show they are too baseless to mention.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r1.anchor: Âyette bu delillerin zikredilmemesi, onların anılmaya bile değmeyecek kadar temelsiz olduğunu göstermektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r2.claim: Abraham's question about disputing over God points to the absurdity of their claims that He has partners.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r2.anchor: de onların iddialarının saçmalığına işaret etmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r3.claim: Although unstated directly, the people's threat that their gods would become angry and punish Abraham is inferred; Abraham disregards it but fears God, whose knowledge encompasses all and whose will governs harm and benefit.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r3.anchor: iyi bir mümin olarak, ilmi her şeyi kuşatan ve bu suretle

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r4.claim: By asking whether they still fail to take heed, Abraham urges rational comparison between idolatry and the monotheism he proved, so they may recognize truth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:80/r4.anchor: doğru öncüllere dayalı aklî değerlendirme ve mukayese yapmaya, bu suretle hakikati bulup tanımaya çağırmıştır

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.claim: The reference to Abraham and later prophets asserts that they invited people to Muhammad’s same message; Muhammad must follow their guidance and leave rejecters to themselves, since he must preach but cannot force belief.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.anchor: His responsibility is to only preach and he is not liable to force people to accept guidance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.claim: Abraham is singled out because Israelites and Ishmaelites both claimed him as patriarch and guide while attributing their inherited religious practices to him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.anchor: both the Israelites and the Ishmaelites regarded him as their patriarch and spiritual leader.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.claim: Judaism, Christianity, and Ishmaelite polytheism are later fabrications with no connection to Abraham; Muhammad’s mission revives and completes Abraham’s religion for his descendants.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.anchor: it was also essential to make it evident to the Ishmaelites that the religion of polytheism they have adopted is their own fabrication

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.claim: After Abraham’s disavowal, his people threaten him with their deities’ wrath; Islahi explains that this fear reflects polytheism’s foundation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.anchor: Since polytheism is based on fear, they began to threaten and warn him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.claim: Abraham’s people did not deny God but associated partners with him; Islahi generalizes that nations err through corrupting monotheism rather than denying God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.anchor: his people never denied God; they only associated partners with him. And this is not something specific to his people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.claim: Abraham says the supposed deities cannot harm him unless God wills, displaying trust in God; Shu‘ayb’s parallel shows even sincere aims require divine help through trials.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p67/.anchor: These words showed his tremendous trust in God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.claim: The grand words Abraham utters in 6:79–80 are prophetic, confirming that the celestial argument occurred after his appointment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p69/.anchor: The grand words uttered in these verses by him can only be said by a

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p332/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p332/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p332/r1.claim: These five readers geminate the nūn in أتحاجوني and تأمروني; Nafi and Ibn Amir read both with a light nūn.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p332/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي: أتحاجوني، وتأمروني مشددتين.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p332/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p332/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p332/r2.claim: The light reading deletes the second of two nūns to avoid gemination; the first remains because it marks inflection and the subject, while the second is expendable.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p332/r2.anchor: فحذفا الثانية من المثلين كراهة التضعيف

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p332/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p332/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p332/r3.claim: Arabic also resolves repeated sounds by deletion or substitution; poetry and Sībawayh's report of a reader support deleting the second nūn, a dialect attributed by some Basrans to Ghatafan.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p332/r3.anchor: وزعم بعض البصريين في حذف هذه النون أنها لغة لغطفان

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p332/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p332/r4.speaker: الكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p332/r4.claim: The source also notes that Kisai alone read هداني.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p143/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p143/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p143/r1.claim: The doubled nūn in أتحاجونني comes from the indicative nūn plus the object nūn before yāʾ, assimilated together; the lighter reading drops one nūn to avoid the pair, as in poetry and تبشرون.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p143/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن شدد أن الأصل فيه أتحاجونني بنونين

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p143/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p143/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p143/r2.claim: For وقد هدان, imāla is justified because the form derives from yāʾ and preserves that origin after the pronoun suffix; tafkhim follows the surface form.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p143/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ وقد هدان ﴾ يقرأ بالإمالة والتفخيم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p260/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p260/r1.speaker: عاصم عن أبي بكر، ابن عامر، حمزة، الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p260/r1.claim: These readers give rāʾ and hamza kasra in رأى; readings before a following quiescent consonant vary by reader and transmission, with full fatḥa, mixed vowels, and in one report kasra on both.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p260/r1.anchor: وقرأ عاصم فى رواية أبى بكر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائى / رءا / بكسر الراء والهمزة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p260/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p260/r2.speaker: ابن كثير، أبو عمرو، عاصم، حمزة، الكسائي، نافع، ابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p260/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai read أتحاجوني with a doubled nūn; Nafi and Ibn Amir use a light nūn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p260/r2.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائى / أتحجونى / و ﴿ تأمروني ﴾ مشددتين

IBNMUJAHID:v1p260/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p260/r3.speaker: الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p260/r3.claim: Al-Kisai reads هدان with imāla on dāl; the other readers use fatḥa.

QIRAAT-ER:6:80:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:80:5#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:80:5#1/r1.claim: The heavy nūn in a-tuḥājjūnnī is presented as the standard reading and adds emphasis to the challenge.
QIRAAT-ER:6:80:5#1/r1.anchor: Heavy nūn (nūn mushaddada) — emphasizes confrontation, standard reading

QIRAAT-ER:6:80:5#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:80:5#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:80:5#2/r1.claim: The light nūn reading a-tuḥājjūnī removes emphasis and softens the confrontational tone.
QIRAAT-ER:6:80:5#2/r1.anchor: Light nūn (nūn mukhaffafa) — drops emphasis, softens the accusatory tone

QIRAAT-ER:6:80:10#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:80:10#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:80:10#1/r1.claim: This variant retains the full yāʾ in hadānī at pause, extending the pronoun for clarity.
QIRAAT-ER:6:80:10#1/r1.anchor: Full yāʾ retained — Ten Readers variant; extends the pronoun for clarity

QIRAAT-ER:6:80:10#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:80:10#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:80:10#2/r1.claim: At pause the form has nūn quiescent, while connected reading retains hadānī; this is a phonetic adaptation.
QIRAAT-ER:6:80:10#2/r1.anchor: Pausal form: nūn sākina at waqf, full -nī in waṣl — phonetic adaptation

QIRAAT-ER:6:80:10#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:80:10#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:80:10#3/r1.claim: Imāla tilts the fatḥa on dāl toward kasra without changing the meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:6:80:10#3/r1.anchor: Imāla (vowel tilting): fatḥa on dāl tilted toward kasra — dialectal phonetic variant

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r5.claim: الغمرة is overwhelming distress; its root image is water covering something, with poetry illustrating both the word and its plural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r5.anchor: الغمرة الشدة المذهلة وأصلها في غمرة الماء وهي ما يغطي الشيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r6.claim: فرادى means one by one; فراد with tanwin is a Tamim dialect, while forms and derivations differ among grammarians.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p560/r6.anchor: فرادى: الألف فيه للتأنيث ومعناها فردا فردا، ويقال فيه فراد منونا على وزن فعال وهي لغة تميم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r2.claim: The reciprocal disputation concerns God's unity; the opponents rely on inherited custom and threats from idols, while Abraham answers that decisive proof has guided him and their argument is futile.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r2.anchor: والمعنى وحاجه قومه في توحيد الله ونفي الشركاء عنه منكرين لذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan compares the idol-threat to the people of Hud claiming one of their gods had afflicted him; the cited example is a threat of harm from a deity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r3.anchor: كقول: قوم هود إن نقول إلا اعتراك بعض آلهتنا بسوء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r4.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir, in Hisham’s transmission, read the address with a light nūn; the underlying form has the indicative nūn and the protective nūn, with grammarians disputing which is omitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر بخلاف عن هشام أتحاجوني بتخفيف النون وأصله بنونين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r5.speaker: مكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r5.claim: Makki calls the light reading an ugly, distant deletion that is acceptable in poetry but, he says, unnecessary in Qur'an; Abu Hayyan rejects this criticism and notes it may be a Ghatafan dialect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r5.anchor: وقول مكي ليس بالمرتضى، وقيل: التخفيف لغة لغطفان، وقرأ باقي السبعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r6.claim: The other canonical readers retain the doubled nūn by assimilation to avoid two consecutive moving identical letters; full separation is possible in ordinary speech but not read here.
