ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة بتشديد النون أصله أتحاجونني فأدغم هروبا من استثقال المثلين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r7.claim: “In God” attaches to the second verb in the reciprocal construction, not the first; the circumstantial clause says they debate despite God's having already guided Abraham, making their case futile.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p568#2/r7.anchor: وفي الله متعلق بأتحاجوني لا بقوله وحاجه قومه والمسألة من باب الإعمال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r1.speaker: الكفار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r1.claim: The disbelievers reportedly threatened that their gods might afflict Abraham with leprosy or disease because he insulted and belittled them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r1.anchor: حكي أن الكفار قالوا لإبراهيم عليه السلام: أما خفت أن تصيبك آلهتنا ببرص أو داء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r2.claim: Abraham says the idols have neither power nor independence, so they cannot frighten him; “mā” may mean the things associated with God or those whom they associate with God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r2.anchor: لست أخاف الذي تشركون به لأنه لا قدرة له ولا غنى عنده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya treats “unless my Lord wills something” as a disconnected exception: Abraham fears only a harm God wills, not harm caused by powerless idols; al-Hawfi agrees.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطية استثناء ليس من الأول ولما كانت قوة الكلام أنه لا يخاف ضرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the exception as connected to the general times covered by the negation: Abraham fears no idol at any time unless God wills a frightening harm through it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r4.anchor: إلا وقت مشيئة ربي شيئا يخاف فحذف الوقت يعني لا أخاف معبوداتكم في وقت قط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows connected or disconnected exception, and for the connected reading takes it from circumstances, meaning “except in the state in which my Lord wills.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r5.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون متصلا ومنقطعا إلا أنه جعله متصلا مستثنى من الأحوال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r6.claim: “Something” is accusative either as an object or as a cognate accusative meaning “a willing.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r6.anchor: وانتصب شيئا على المصدر أي مشيئة أو على المفعول به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r7.claim: God's knowledge of all events explains why a feared harm cannot be ruled out under either reading of the exception; “knowledge” is an accusative specification transformed from the subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r7.anchor: وسع ربي كل شيء علما ذكر عقيب الاستثناء سعة علم الله في تعلقه بجميع الكوائن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r8.claim: The closing question rebukes their heedlessness in worshiping things that neither harm nor benefit, and urges them to consider Abraham’s proof against their divinity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r8.anchor: تنبيه لهم على غفلتهم حيث عبدوا ما لا يضر ولا ينفع، وأشركوا بالله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses the question as a call to distinguish sound from corrupt reasoning and the capable from the incapable; al-Razi says denying rivals does not itself entail punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p569/r9.anchor: أفلا تتذكرون فتميزوا بين الصحيح والفاسد والقادر والعاجز

ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r1.speaker: الربيع
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r1.claim: Al-Rabiʿ glosses Abraham's people's dispute as arguing with him; alternatively they began combating him over monotheism with false traditional arguments and threats.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r1.anchor: أي خاصمون كما قال الربيع أو شرعوا في مغالبته في أمر التوحيد تارة بإيراد أدلة فاسدة واقعة في حضيض التقليد

ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r2.claim: Abraham rebukes them for attempting debate despite their limited standing, the matter's importance, the opponent's strength, and the clarity of truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r2.anchor: منكرا عليهم محاجتهم له عليه السلام مع قصورهم عن تلك المرتبة وعزة المطلب وقوة الخصم ووضوح الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r3.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r3.claim: Nafiʿ and Ibn Amir, in one transmission, read the doubled nūn lightly, deleting one of the two nūns in 'do you dispute with me?'.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر في رواية ابن ذ : وان بتخفيف النون ففيه حذف أحدى النونين

ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r4.claim: Sibawayh says the deleted nūn is the indicative ending; the retained nūn is needed in a kasra form before yā, deletion is attested elsewhere, and the pronoun nūn is not protective.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r4.anchor: فقيل : نون الرفع وهو مذهب شيبويه ورجح بأن الحاجة دعت إلى نون مكسورة من أجل الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r5.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash identifies the deleted nūn as the protective nūn, preferring deletion of the redundant source of phonetic weight.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r5.anchor: وقيل نون الوقاية وهو مذهب الأخفش ورجح بأنها الزائدة التي حصل بها الثقل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r6.claim: 'He guided me' is a circumstantial clause strengthening Abraham's refusal to debate: divine guidance and support should make them cease arguing and make him disregard their challenge.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r6.anchor: كونه عليه الصلاة والسلام مهديا من جهة الله تعالى ومؤيدا من عنده سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r7.speaker: some exegetes
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r7.claim: Some take the guidance to mean God showed Abraham how to establish the proof of divine unity against them.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r7.anchor: والمراد وقد هدان إلى إقامة الدليل عليكم بوحدانيته عز شأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r8.speaker: some exegetes
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r8.claim: Another explanation says Abraham had hypothetically followed their path, then saw its total invalidity; neither reading implies that he was previously astray or ignorant of God.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r8.anchor: وقيل : هدان إلى الحق بعد ما سلكت طريقكم بالفرض والتقدير وتبين بطلانها تبينا تاما

ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Abraham's statement that he does not fear their gods answers his people's threat of harm from their idols, comparable to the threat made to Hud.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r9.anchor: جواب كما روي عن ابن جريج عما خوفوه عليه السلام من إصابة مكروه من جهة معبودهم الباطل

ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r10.speaker: some exegetes
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r10.claim: The threat may have been for abandoning their worship, for mocking and belittling the idols, or after Abraham damaged them; a report describes him mocking idols made by Azar by throwing them into a river and telling them to drink.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r10.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار أنه عليه السلام لما شب وكبر جعل آزر يصنع الأصنام فيعطيها له ليبيعها

ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r11.claim: The object in 'what you associate' may be relative, with its deleted antecedent referring to what they associate with God; it may also be an indefinite modifier or a verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r11.anchor: وما موصولة اسمية حذف عائدها والضمير المجرور لله تعالى أي لا أخاف الذي تشركونه به سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r12.claim: The exception may be connected: Abraham fears harm from their idols only at a time when God wills it, so the idols have no independent agency; it may instead be an unconnected exception meaning he fears his Lord's willing that he fear them.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r12.anchor: والاستثناء متصل في رأي وشيأ مفعول به أو مفعول مطلق أي لا أخاف ما تشركون به في وقت من الاوقات

ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r13.speaker: ابن الأنباري وابن جني
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r13.claim: Ibn al-Anbari allows temporal use of an explicit verbal noun but not an implicit one; Ibn Jinni does not distinguish them and permits both.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r13.anchor: ومنع ذلك ابن الانباري مفرقا بين المصدر الصريح فيجوز نصبه على الظرفية وغير الصريح فلا يجوز فيه ذلك وابن جني لا يفرق

ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r14.claim: Calling God 'my Lord' signals that any willed harm would carry a nurturing purpose, or Abraham's submission to God's rule and ownership.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p204#2/r14.anchor: وفي التعرض لعنوان الربوبية مع الإضافة إلى ضميره عليه السلام إشارة إلى أن مشيئته تلك إن وقعت غير خالية عن مصلحة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p205/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205/r1.claim: God's all-encompassing knowledge explains the exception: He may know a reason to send harm through the idols; 'knowledge' is either specification converted from the subject or a cognate-like verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205/r1.anchor: كأنه تعليل للاستثناء أي أحاط بكل شيء علما فلا يبعد أن يكون في علمه سبحانه انزال المكروه بي من جهتها

ALUSI-FULL:v7p205/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205/r2.claim: Naming 'my Lord' instead of using a pronoun reinforces the point and gives pleasure in mentioning God.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205/r2.anchor: وفي الإظهار في موضع الإضمار تأكيد للمعنى المذكور واستلذاذ بذكره تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v7p205/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205/r3.claim: The question asks whether they will not remember that their idols cannot cause harm or benefit; 'remember' suggests their inability is already embedded in reason and only needs prompting.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p205/r3.anchor: وفي إيراد التذكر دون التفكر ونحوه إشارة إلى أن أمر آلهتهم مركوز في العقول لا يتوقف إلا على التذكير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r1.claim: After Abraham had grown beyond the slayers' reach, his father Azar made idols and gave them to him to sell; Abraham mocked them as harmful and useless, then struck their heads in a river and told them to drink, spreading mockery among his people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r1.anchor: ولما رجع إبراهيم عليه السلام إلى أبيه، وصار من الشباب بحالة سقط عنه طمع الذباحين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r2.claim: His people argued and disputed with him; ḥājjahu means argued or contended.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r2.anchor: فحاجه أي خاصمه وجادله قومه في دينه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r3.speaker: أهل المدينة وابن عامر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r3.claim: They read atuhājjūnī with a light nūn; others geminate it by assimilating one of the two nūns, while the light reading omits one for ease. Abraham asks why they dispute monotheism after his guidance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r3.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة وابن عامر بتخفيف النون، وقرأ الآخرون بتشديدها إدغاما لإحدى النونين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r4.claim: His people warned that disparaging idols would bring illness or madness, but Abraham says he does not fear what they associate with God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r4.anchor: وذلك أنهم قالوا له: احذر الأصنام فإنا نخاف أن تمسك بسوء من خبل أو جنون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r5.claim: The exception in unless my Lord wills is disconnected: if God wills some harm, it occurs; it is not an exception to Abraham's fear of idols.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r5.anchor: وليس هذا باستثناء عن الأول بل هو استثناء منقطع، معناه لكن إن يشأ ربي شيئا أي سوء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r6.claim: God's knowledge encompasses everything; the question urges the people to reflect.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p163/r6.anchor: وسع ربي كل شيء علما} أي: أحاط علمه بكل شيء، {أفلا تتذكرون}

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r2.claim: His people dispute divine unity; Nafi and Ibn Amir, with a qualification for Hisham, lighten the nūn in a-tuḥājjūnī.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r2.anchor: وخاصموه في التوحيد. { قال أتحاجونى فى الله } في وحدانيته سبحانه وتعالى.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r3.claim: God guided him to unity; he does not fear idols because they cannot themselves harm or benefit.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r3.anchor: وقد هدان } إلى توحيده. { ولا أخاف ما تشركون به } أي لا أخاف معبوداتكم في وقت لأنها لا تضر بنفسها

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r4.claim: The exception means God may cause harm through them, answering their threat and warning of His punishment; God's all-encompassing knowledge explains the possibility.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r4.anchor: إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا } أن يصيبني بمكروه من جهتها، ولعله جواب لتخويفهم إياه من آلهتهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r5.claim: The challenge to remember asks people to distinguish sound from false reasoning and the capable from the incapable.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:79-80/r5.anchor: أفلا تتذكرون } فتميزوا بين الصحيح والفاسد والقادر والعاجز.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p660/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p660/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p660/r6.claim: Abraham’s people argued that they would keep worshipping their inherited idols and threatened him with calamity if he did not stop opposing them.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p660/r6.anchor: بأنهم لا ينفكون عن عبا تها لأنهم وجدوا آباءهم كذلك , وأنه إن لم يرجع عن الكلام فيها أصابته ببعض النوازل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p660/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p660/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p660/r7.claim: Their challenge is especially feeble after the clear proofs; the narrative leaves their arguments unstated as unworthy of mention and highlights Abraham’s answer.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p660/r7.anchor: نزه المقام عن ذكرها , إشارة إلى أنها بحيث لا يستحق الذكر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r1.claim: Abraham says he hopes in and fears God, who alone is able to cause benefit or harm.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r2.claim: He denies fearing the idols because they are powerless; this implies that God alone can cause harm, and the argument reverses what the idolaters fear.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r2.anchor: ولا أرجوه لهداية ولا إضلال ولا غيرهما لأنه عاجز

BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r3.claim: The contrast is an instance of rhetorical ellipsis: God’s power to guide implies His power to misguide, while the idols’ inability to harm implies their inability to benefit.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r3.anchor: فأثبت لله القدرة بالهداية لأنها أشرف , وطوى الإضلال لدلالتها ودلالة ما نفي في جانب الشركاء عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r4.claim: Abraham’s qualification “unless my Lord wills something” is no expression of doubt: only God knows hidden outcomes, and He can empower even an otherwise powerless being if He wills.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r4.anchor: فأنا لا أخاف في الحقيقة غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r5.claim: God’s encompassing knowledge entails power to remove every impediment if He chooses to empower the powerless; Abraham withholds certainty only because outcomes belong to God’s knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r5.anchor: فهو إذا أراد إقدار العاجز أزال عنه كل مانع من القدرة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r6.claim: “Will you not remember?” calls them back to their inborn capacity to distinguish truth: idols cannot help or harm and are themselves manufactured.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p661/r6.anchor: أي يقع منكم تذكر , فتميزوا بين الحق والباطل

DURR-FULL:v3p307/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r1.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r1.claim: ‘His people argued with him’ means they disputed with Abraham.
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r1.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس في قوله {وحاجه قومه} يقول: خاصموه

DURR-FULL:v3p307/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r2.claim: The verb ‘are you arguing with me’ means ‘are you disputing with me.’
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {أتحاجوني} قال: أتخاصموني

DURR-FULL:v3p307/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r3.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r3.claim: ‘Asim read the verb with a doubled nūn.
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r3.anchor: عن عاصم أنه قرأ (أتحاجوني) مشددة النون

DURR-FULL:v3p307/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r4.claim: Abraham’s people called him to worship another god and threatened him with their idols; he answered that he would not fear them, then challenged their failure to fear their unsupported association of partners with God.
DURR-FULL:v3p307/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {وحاجه قومه} قال: دعوا مع الله إلها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r1.claim: Of the omitted yāʾs in this surah, Abu Amr retains the yāʾ in وقد هدان when connected but drops it at pause.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r1.anchor: فأثبتها أبو عمرو فى الوصل وحذفها فى الوقف

IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r2.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r2.claim: Nafi retains the yāʾ in connection through Ismail ibn Jafar and Ibn Jammaz, but Qalun, Warsh, and al-Musayyibi omit it in both positions; the others omit it throughout.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p275/r2.anchor: واختلف عن نافع فأثبتها فى الوصل فى رواية إسماعيل بن جعفر وابن جماز وحذفها فى الوصل والوقف فى رواية قالون وورش والمسيبى

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.claim: When light or heavy emphatic nūn follows a singular jussive verb, its final consonant takes fatḥa; kasra or ḍamma would confuse gender or number.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.anchor: اعلم أن فعل الواحد إذا كان مجزوما فلحقته الخفيفة والثقيلة حركت المجزوم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.claim: A singular indicative verb takes fatḥa before emphatic nūn so it is not confused with the plural form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.anchor: وإذا كان فعل الواحد مرفوعا ثم لحقته النون

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.claim: With a dual indicative verb, heavy nūn replaces the dual nūn but leaves the alif, preserving the dual marker; light nūn cannot follow the alif because it is not assimilated.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.anchor: وإذا كان فعل الاثنين مرفوعا وأدخلت النون الثقيلة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.claim: When emphatic nūn is added to an indicative plural verb, the indicative nūn is deleted, avoiding a sequence of three nūns or disliked doubling.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.anchor: وإذا كان فعل الجميع مرفوعا ثم أدخلت فيه النون الخفيفة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.speaker: بعض القراء وأهل المدينة
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.claim: Some readers read أتحاجوني, and the Medinans read فبم تبشرون, reducing doubled nūn because they found gemination heavy.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.speaker: عمرو بن معد يكرب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.claim: ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib’s فليني, for فلينني, is poetic evidence for dropping one nūn under the same pressure against gemination.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.anchor: وقال عمرو بن معد يكرب # % تراه كالثغام

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.claim: An unvocalized feminine singular yāʾ is dropped before emphatic nūn to avoid adjacent sukūns; in indicative forms the indicative nūn drops and the yāʾ remains.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.claim: For a masculine plural, the indicative nūn drops before emphatic nūn and the wāw remains, as it does in the imperative.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.anchor: ومن ذلك قولهم للجميع اضربن زيدا وأكرمن عمرا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.claim: When the attached pronoun marker would meet a following hamzat al-waṣl or article, it is vocalized to prevent two sukūns, with the same vowel used before emphatic nūn.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأحوالالحروفالتيقبلالنونا.anchor: وذلك قولك ارضون زيدا تريد الجميع

NASHR:v1p350/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p350/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p350/r1.claim: The three lengths apply only to readers who choose full length elsewhere in this chapter; those who choose short length must shorten here, while medium readers may use medium or short but not full.
NASHR:v1p350/r1.anchor: والتحقيق في ذلك أن يقال: إن هذه الأوجه لا تسوغ إلا لمن ذهب إلى الإشباع في حروف المد من هذا الباب

NASHR:v1p350/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p350/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p350/r2.claim: For Abu Amr’s large assimilation, all three lengths are allowed with incidental gemination, though most readers shorten; Ibn al-Qassāʿ reports madd and medium length.
NASHR:v1p350/r2.anchor: والعارض المشدد نحو (الليل لباسا. كيف فعل. الليل رأى. بالخير لقضي) عند أبي عمرو في الإدغام الكبير

NASHR:v1p350/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p350/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p350/r3.claim: The chapter’s rule begins by distinguishing the madd condition from its cause; each may be necessary or incidental, stable or changed, and strong or weak, as the listed examples illustrate.
NASHR:v1p350/r3.anchor: تقدم أن شرط المد حرفه، وأن سببه موجبه. (فالشرط) قد يكون لازما فيلزم في كل حال نحو

NASHR:v2p266/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p266/r5.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p266/r5.claim: The Madinan readers, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr open the yāʾ in إني أخاف and إني أراك.
NASHR:v2p266/r5.anchor: إني أخاف، إني أراك فتحهما المدنيان، وابن كثير وأبو عمرو

NASHR:v2p266/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p266/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وقنبل
NASHR:v2p266/r10.claim: Abu Jaafar and Abu Amr do not affirm the extra yāʾ in وصل; Yaqub affirms it in both states, as does Qunbul in Ibn Shanabudh’s route.
NASHR:v2p266/r10.anchor: وقد هدان ولا أثبتها وصلا أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وأثبتها في الحالتين يعقوب

BURHAN:v2p395/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p395/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
BURHAN:v2p395/r1.claim: Abu al-Baqa treats uluwwan in “exalted with great exaltation” as a verbal noun in place of ta'aliyan; al-Raghib agrees, while allowing that it can be a verbal noun elsewhere too.
BURHAN:v2p395/r1.anchor: قال أبو البقاء هو موضع تعاليا لانه مصدر قوله ﴿ وتعالى ﴾ ويجوز ان يقع مصدرا

BURHAN:v2p395/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p395/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p395/r2.claim: The wording avoids the tafa''ul form because it can suggest effort or affectation, as it does with human speakers.
BURHAN:v2p395/r2.anchor: وانما عدل عنه لان لفظ التفاعل من التكلف كما يكون من البشر

BURHAN:v2p395/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p395/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p395/r5.claim: In the exception, shay'an may be an emphatic cognate object, or it may mean an affair or clarification placed where a verbal noun would stand; this also challenges the claim that a general object of will must be omitted.
BURHAN:v2p395/r5.anchor: واما قوله تعالى ﴿ إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا ﴾ فيحتمل ان يكون ﴿ شيئا ﴾ من تأكيد الفعل بالمصدر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r1.claim: Calling a king’s hooves uncracked lies between simile and metaphor: it implies a king rather than a rough, lowly servant.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r1.anchor: هو في حد التشبيه والاستعارة لأن المعنى على أن الأظلاف لمن تزيى بالملك

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r2.speaker: أبو بكر بن دريد
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r2.claim: Ibn Durayd gives جاءنا حافيا متشقق الأظلاف as an insulting expression, supporting the negative association of cracked hooves.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r2.anchor: أبا بكر بن دريد قال في أول الباب الذي وضعه للاستعارة يقولون للرجل إذا عابوه جاءنا حافيا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r3.claim: The poet applies تولب, originally a donkey’s foal, to a human child in a depiction of poverty and misery.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r3.anchor: فأجرى التولب على ولد المرأة وهو لولد الحمار في الأصل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r4.claim: Animal descriptions intensify the portrayal of the poor woman’s distress; another poet similarly calls disheveled, wretched people foals.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r4.anchor: والعادة في مثل ذلك الصفة بأوصاف البهائم ليكون ابلغ في سوء الحالة وشدة الاختلال

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r5.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī rejects al-Mufaḍḍal’s reading جذعا with ذ, insisting on جدعا with د, meaning poorly fed, and rebukes his protest.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r5.anchor: أنشد المفضل تصمت بالماء تولبا جذعا بالذال المعجمة فأنكره الأصمعي وقال إنما هو تصمت بالماء تولبا جدعا وهو السيء الغذاء

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r6.claim: An Arab’s question كيف الطلا وأمه alludes to likening the newborn to a gazelle’s young, making the expression informative and apt.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r6.anchor: قول الأعرابي كيف الطلا وأمه فمن جنس المفيد أيضا لأنه أشار إلى شيء من تشبيه المولود بولد الظبي

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r7.claim: In the anecdote, the question follows the man’s shift from anger as hunger subsides; his wife says he is starving, and they weep for him.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r7.anchor: بعد أن انصرف عن السخط إلى الرضي وبعد أن سكن عنه فورة الجوع الذي دعاه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r8.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r8.claim: Calling the rooster’s group قوم grants it a rational, human-like status, signaled by the preceding pronoun هم and the rational pronoun used for it.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r8.anchor: قدم تتزيلها منزلتهم فقال هم فأتى بضمير من يعقل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r9.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r9.claim: Once brave men are presented as actual lions, the adjective follows the nonrational lion form الضارية rather than the human plural الضارون.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p29/r9.anchor: فتقول الضارية ولا تقول الضارون البتة

DAMGHANI:v1p35/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p35/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p35/r1.claim: The second use of illā resembles an exception but resumes the statement after a pause; in 6:80 and 7:188, what God wills may befall the speaker.
DAMGHANI:v1p35/r1.anchor: الثاني : إلا وهو الذي يشبه الاستثناء ولكنه استئناف . قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r1.speaker: أبو زكريا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r1.claim: Illa is fundamentally the particle of exception and the most established and widely used of the exceptive tools.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r1.anchor: قال أبو زكريا : وللاستثناء أدوات موضوعة فأشدها استيلاء على باب الاستثناء وأكثرها استعمالا إلا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r2.speaker: أبو زكريا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r2.claim: Other exception forms resemble illa; the entry lists the nouns سوى, غير, بيد, ميد, the verbs ليس, لا يكون, عدا, and the particles حاشا, خلا.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r2.anchor: فمن الأدوات التي استثنى بها لشبهها بإلا أسماء وأفعال وحروف ، فمن الأسماء : سوى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r3.speaker: أنشدوا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r3.claim: Illa can also carry the meaning of waw, as illustrated by the line about every brother parting from his brother except the two stars.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r3.anchor: وقد تقع إلا بمعنى ' الواو ' ، وأنشدوا من ذلك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r4.claim: The first Qur'anic use is exception, illustrated by exclusions in 25:69, 29:14, and 43:67.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r4.anchor: أحدها : الاستثناء . ومنه قوله تعالى في الفرقان : ﴿ ويخلد فيه مهانا إلا من تاب وآمن ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r5.claim: The entry classifies illa in 6:80 as an استئناف, a fresh clause; it groups several other examples under the same heading.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r5.anchor: والثاني : الاستئناف . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام : ﴿ ولا أخاف ما تشركون به إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r6.claim: A third Qur'anic use of illa is بمعنى غير, as in the statements that there are no gods except God and that they taste no death except the first death.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p123/r6.anchor: والثالث : بمعنى غير . ومنه قوله تعالى
